spec: DESIGN.md — firmware: an emulator-centric answer, live declarations against packaged identities
description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical firmware serializations (atlas/contract.py firmware_contract, identification_contract) out, asserted with exact equality. A firmware answer is about EMULATORS: each installed core states what it wants, where each file goes as an absolute path, and what is actually lying there. Two axes stay apart — need (required/optional) is what an emulator asks for, checked (verified/mismatch/unchecked/unknown/not-comparable/unrecognised) is what the machine answers, and 'we did not look' never collapses into 'we looked and cannot tell'. The load-bearing pair is firmware-core-that-declares-nothing-answers-nothing-needed against firmware-core-not-installed-is-unknown-not-nothing: the same empty list, opposite meanings, and only the installed flag plus a caveat tells them apart. Firmware blobs are stated as {md5, sha1, size} because firmware is not text and its identity is exactly what a real file would answer with. A core's requirements list is a conjunction, and one entry may be an 'alternatives' group — a single-key object whose options are full requirements each carrying 'regions', the console regions whose launch it serves, disjoint across the group: one launch needs exactly one option, the running disc's region decides, and a region no option lists has nothing stated for it. A third axis joins them and never merges with either: supplied_by says WHOSE file is at the destination, and it is set exactly when the bytes there equal the bytes the distribution's own preparation step copies in (atlas/data/distribution_supplied.json). It is read whether or not verification was asked for, because a consumer deciding whether a file is safe to delete needs it on a cheap answer too, and it is null wherever nothing was established — not the distribution's copy, no copy list for this distribution, no entry for this destination.

vectors.rationale: The case that decides the model. Gambatte wants gb_bios.bin, SameBoy wants dmg_boot.bin, and the packaged table carries both under one md5. vectors.name: retrodeck-cemus-keys-are-a-packaged-expectation
vectors.rationale: A standalone emulator ships no .info, so what it expects is a packaged card, and the answer says so: declaration 'packaged' with the provenance caveat, never dressed up as a machine read. The destination is the emulator's own probe — Cemu reads its keys at GetUserDataPath('keys.txt') (KeyCache.cpp:63 at 2.6), the flatpak's data home here — resolved through the arrangement's symlink into the BIOS staging path, and what sits there is read live. vectors.name: emudeck-the-launcher-route-carries-the-keys-expectation

The destination is the AppImage's own probe on the host XDG tree (~/.local/share/Cemu/keys.txt), and here nothing sits at it: EmuDeck's installer parks a found keys.txt in the config directory instead (emuDeckCemu.sh), a path the shipped Linux build's key probe never reads — so the honest answer is a missing file at the door the emulator actually opens. vectors.name: retrodeck-beetle-psx-boots-an-image-filed-under-a-hyphenated-name
vectors.rationale: The deployed core on a deployed arrangement: RetroDECK's bios folder is the system directory, and the image in it is filed as SCPH-5502.bin. That is the third of the six names Beetle PSX tries for a PAL console, so the launch starts while the declaration spells scph5502.bin — the answer names the file that is there, keeps the declared row beside it, and states every name the core tries.
